items.title: Victorian election 2026 live results: Jess Wilson vows to ‘bring back hope’ to Victoria after historic victory over Labor
items.author: Stephanie Convery (now) and Josh Taylor (earlier)
items.content:
Follow live updates and results tonight as Jess Wilson becomes state’s 51st premier, with Labor leader Ben Carroll projected to lose seat

Federal politicians largely absent from state election

Just following on from the last post, it is notable that the prime minister, , did not do a press conference with the state premier, , during the campaign, and the federal Liberal leader, , did just one press conference with his state counterpart, , during the campaign.

I give a shoutout to all those Labor party workers who are handing out how-to-votes, the candidates who are working their guts out, but they know that it’s going to be very, very tough.

And we know that this election campaign has been dominated by really the sorts of issues that you get when a government’s been in for more than 10 years.

Continue reading...

items.title: What the World’s Richest Man Did to the World’s Poorest Children
items.author: Nicholas Kristof
items.content: <article>In South Sudan, I discovered more deaths as a result of Elon Musk’s U.S.A.I.D. cuts.</article>

items.title: Two Médecins Sans Frontières staff killed by Israeli strike in Gaza, charity says
items.author: William Christou
items.content:
MSF and head of WHO denounce attack on Gaza City clinic as Israel claims security guards were members of Hamas

Israeli forces have bombed a clinic run by Médecins Sans Frontières in Gaza City, killing two of its staff members, the organisation has said.

MSF said Israel directly struck the clinic, despite the fact that its location was known to the Israeli military and that it was well marked with MSF logos. The organisation denounced the attack and said that with the deaths of the two security guards on Saturday, Israel had killed 17 of its staff members during the war in Gaza.

Continue reading...

items.title: Victorian election 2026: Labor suffers historic defeat as Coalition wins majority government
items.author: Benita Kolovos and Henry Belot
items.content:
Jess Wilson to become state’s first popularly elected female premier as Ben Carroll loses seat in 2026 state election, and Greens and One Nation surge

Victorian Labor has suffered a historic defeat, ending 12 years of government, with the Coalition winning majority government and the Greens securing a record number of seats.

One Nation was on course to win more than 20% of the primary vote, but struggled to pick up lower house seats on a night when huge swings and three- or even four-party contests in many electorates made preference flows difficult to calculate.

Continue reading...

items.title: Argentina fails to block UK-led oil drilling off Falkland Islands
items.author: Press Association
items.content:
International tribunal rules there does not appear to be basis for believing Buenos Aires has jurisdiction on islands

Argentina’s attempt to block oil drilling off the Falkland Islands has been rejected by an international tribunal.

Buenos Aires had called for the international tribunal for the law of the sea (ITLOS) to order a halt to the Sea Lion project, as part of its claim to sovereignty over the Falklands.

Continue reading...

items.title: High-security prisoner used soap to escape despite being handcuffed and chained to officer
items.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
items.content:
Exclusive: inmate from HMP Manchester now back in custody after 13 hours on the run

A prisoner from one of England and Wales’s most dysfunctional high-security jails is believed to have used soap to help escape from officers while visiting a hospital for treatment.

The 36-year-old detained at HMP Manchester managed to slip away despite being cuffed and chained to an officer, sources told the Guardian. He is believed to have lathered his metal cuff with liquid soap and slipped his hand out while being given privacy to use a bathroom.

Continue reading...

items.title: US oligarchs enriched by ‘transactional’ Trump face fierce scrutiny in new Congress
items.author: Peter Stone in Washington
items.content:
Democrats pledge aggressive investigations into Trump-allied billionaires and how president’s policies have boosted their bottom lines

For an elite circle of Donald Trump billionaire allies who lavished tensof millions of dollars on his campaign, vanity projects and crypto ventures, his second administration has boosted their bottom lines through lax oversight, tax breaks, federal contracts and other perks.

But with Democrats winning control of Congress in the midterms, House and Senate investigations are being planned for 2027 into several Maga oligarchs in hi-tech and crypto industries, examining how their firms and the president benefited from his “transactional” governing style, according to Democratic lawmakers and scholars.

Continue reading...

items.title: Deal with Epstein lawyer and accountant could block victims’ other claims, experts warn
items.author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
items.content:
Concern that settlement to resolve suit against pair may stymie legal claims that involve child sexual abuse material

As the clock ticks toward final settlement for a sex-trafficking-related lawsuit against Jeffrey Epstein’s accountant and attorney, some experts are expressing concern that the agreement might stymie survivors’ search for justice in other litigation involving child sexual abuse images.

The suit involves Darren Indyke and Richard D Kahn, who for decades worked as Epstein’s personal lawyer and accountant respectively. Both men also serve as executors of Epstein’s estate. Indyke and Kahn have insisted they knew nothing about Epstein’s crimes and have rejected allegations of wrongdoing.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Please can I have one more picture’: the US airmen accused of child sexual abuse in UK who avoided British trial
items.author: Rob Evans, Harry Davies, Louisa Loveluck and Emine Sinmaz
items.content:
Guardian investigation reveals US military personnel, including ‘multi-child molester’, convicted in courts martial

When Jacob Ozbirn, an American airman, drove to a country lane near a Derbyshire hotel one summer’s evening, he was expecting to meet a 12-year-old girl he had been grooming for sex.

In the previous days, he had sent explicit messages to her and two other girls, encouraging them to send him naked photos, despite having been told by all three that they were aged 12 or 13.

Continue reading...

items.title: My Six Months With Saddam Hussein
items.author: George Piro
items.content: <article>As the Iraqi dictator’s chief F.B.I. interrogator, I learned how much pre-Iraq war profilers got wrong about him.</article>

items.title: Drones ‘swarmed’ US army base at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk in November
items.author: Harry Taylor
items.content:
Personnel told to take cover after ‘suspected unauthorised activity’ of six drones that were repelled but not recovered

Drones reportedly swarmed a US army base in Suffolk earlier this month and were not recovered after being repelled.

Personnel at RAF Lakenheath were told to take cover on 13 November after “suspected unauthorised drone activity”. The US air force confirmed the so-called Charlie alert at the time, the second-highest threat level, but released few details. Sirens could be heard at the base. Iran is suspected of being involved.

Continue reading...

items.title: Retail Therapy
items.author: Melissa Kirsch
items.content: <article>It’s holiday shopping season. Do not panic.</article>

items.title: Spain to vote in election that could put far right in power for first time since Franco
items.author: Sam Jones in Madrid
items.content:
Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez’s high-stakes gamble could end in defeat to a coalition including the far-right Vox

Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday to vote in a high-stakes snap general election that could put a far-right party in government for the first time since the country’s return to democracy after the death of Gen FranciscoFranco in 1975.

Although the next election was not due until summer next year, Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called the vote in October after three rightwing and far-right parties voted down the emergency legislation that his government had proposed to address the country’s housing crisis.

Continue reading...

items.title: DWP cyber incident ‘probably an attack’, says former UK chief technology officer
items.author: Kevin Rawlinson
items.content:
Government took down pensions and benefits portal on Thursday but said regular payments will not be affected

A serious cyber incident that forced ministers to take down online benefits and pension services was “probably an attack”, the UK’s former chief technology officer has said.

The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable.

Continue reading...

items.title: Pedro Pascal’s Life Began With a Rupture. He’s Still Coming to Terms With It.
items.author: Lulu Garcia-Navarro
items.content: <article>At 51, the actor and “Behemoth!” star is navigating his past and embracing his present. </article>

items.title: Ukraine’s Deep Strikes Grow in Scale and Scope Across Russia and Beyond
items.author: Marc Santora
items.content: <article>A campaign aimed at depriving Moscow’s war machine of fuel, weapons and money has been criticized by the Trump administration.</article>

items.title: Canada’s Arctic Reservists Know the Land. Fewer Young People Do.
items.author: Norimitsu Onishi and Renaud Philippe
items.content: <article>Canada relies on Inuit and First Nations Rangers’ traditional knowledge of the land to protect its most inhospitable corners. But that knowledge is disappearing.</article>

items.title: Woman ‘traumatised’ by Sainsbury’s shoplifting ban after staff facial recognition error
items.author: Jessica Murray and Rosie Peters-McDonald
items.content:
Monia Indge, 58, who has terminal cancer, escorted from supermarket after staff using FaceWatch technology misidentified her

A woman with terminal cancer has been left “traumatised and violated” after being falsely accused of shoplifting and banned from Sainsbury’s by staff using facial recognition technology.

Monia Indge, 58, was shopping with her husband in the Walters Yard branch of Sainsbury’s in Bromley on 7 November when she was suddenly told to leave by a member of staff who told her she was “banned for life” from the store.

Continue reading...

items.title: Freed From a Notorious Syrian Prison, but Still Trapped by Its Terror
items.author: Raja Abdulrahim
items.content: <article>Ahmed al-Shalh expected to perish in Sednaya prison. Abruptly released after a decade, he reveled in marriage and fatherhood but struggled to shake his ghosts.</article>

items.title: Palestinian tells of ‘devastating’ struggle after being made redundant by EU in Gaza
items.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
items.content:
Mohammad Baraka unable to access redundancy pay for almost 20 years’ service as family’s situation becomes ‘increasingly desperate’

A Palestinian man who worked for the EU in Gaza has told of a “devastating” struggle to survive after he was made redundant by bosses in Brussels.

He was let go last year after being evacuated to Egypt but his redundancy payment was made to an account to which he has no access. “My family’s situation has become increasingly desperate,” said Mohammad Baraka, a former staffer at the EU border assistance mission (EUBam).

Continue reading...

items.title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
items.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
items.content:
Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed him

They are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals.

But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault, 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company.

Continue reading...

items.title: Yuri and I used to play football together. Then I spotted his name among Russia’s war dead
items.author: Pjotr Sauer
items.content:
I had no idea he had gone to fight in Ukraine and without hacked data I would probably never have learned of his death

One evening, after weeks spent counting Russia’s war dead, I began looking for names I might recognise.

My colleagues and I had been working our way through more than 11m death certificates leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, and identifying nearly half a million Russian soldiers who had died in the war in Ukraine.

Continue reading...

items.title: Australia’s east coast deluged by storms as roads flood and damaging winds forecast for NSW and Victoria
items.author: Australian Associated Press
items.content:
Severe weather and flood watch warnings are in place as a storm band moves from central Queensland through NSW to Victoria and Tasmania

The final weekend of Australia’s wettest spring on record for an El Niño year is delivering a deluge of storms and heavy rain.

Severe weather and flood watch warnings were in place across the eastern states as a weather band moves from central Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and Tasmania.

Continue reading...

items.title: Some Americans canceled or postponed Thanksgiving dinners amid power outages and storms.
items.author: Katie Benner, Mack Liederman and Emma Schartz
items.content: <article>Some Americans canceled or postponed Thanksgiving dinners amid power outages and storms. They were rescheduled to Friday, Saturday and beyond.</article>

items.title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
items.author: Keely Aouga
items.content:
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach

The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.

The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.

Continue reading...

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees

OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of ⁠stealing its trade secrets ​and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.

The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.

Continue reading...

items.title: Thousands still without power after storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel
items.author: Edward Helmore and agencies
items.content:
Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia

Skies cleared along the US eastern seaboard on Friday, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region a day earlier.

The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
items.author: Keely Aouga
items.content:
Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’

A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries.

Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’
items.author: Caroline Davies
items.content:
Police are working with agencies across Europe after similar incidents occurred at two other Don Toliver concerts

Greater Manchester police said they were working to identify the suspects and the substance involved during the incident at the Co-op Live Arena on Sunday evening.

Continue reading...

items.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
items.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
items.content:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights

Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.

In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.

Continue reading...

items.title: Jess Wilson’s plan for Melbourne sewage plants risks water and wetlands without bringing debt down, experts say
items.author: Josh Taylor
items.content:
Academic says Victorian Liberal proposal to privatise treatment plants and generate profit with no compromise of services ‘a total furphy’

Experts have warned the Victorian Liberals’ plan to lease Melbourne’s sewage treatment plants is a “smoke and mirrors” way to pay off debt that risks compromising the state’s water resources and crucial wetlands for nearly a century.

Continue reading...

items.title: Labor faces prospect of electoral wipeout in Victoria as voters turn to Liberals and One Nation
items.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
items.content:
Former ALP strategist says Ben Carroll government at risk of losing more than 30 seats in Saturday’s election, to fall behind Pauline Hanson’s party

The Victorian Labor government is facing an electoral wipeout after 12 years in office as the state heads to the polls on Saturday.

Polling during the campaign has consistently pointed to a Coalition victory. The final Newspoll, released on Thursday, showed the Coalition 15 points ahead on a two-party-preferred basis.

Continue reading...

items.title: Momentous decision looms after judges call for Netanyahu charges to be dropped
items.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
items.content:
Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent

The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.

Continue reading...

items.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
items.author: Eromo Egbejule in Lagos
items.content:
What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape

As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.

In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.

Continue reading...

items.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
items.author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
items.content:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Continue reading...

items.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
items.author: Amy Hawkins and Yu-chen Li in Taipei
items.content:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party

Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.

Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.

Continue reading...

items.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
items.author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
items.content:
Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City

Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”

Continue reading...

items.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
items.author: David Batty
items.content:
Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum

In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.

They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

Continue reading...

items.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
items.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
items.content:
Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, a politician charged with murder

It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.

Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.

Continue reading...

items.title: Business
‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
items.content:
The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.

Continue reading...

items.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.author: Rebecca Bailey and agencies
items.content:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

Continue reading...

items.title: Robots will have a staggering economic impact
items.content:
<article>
        Workable humanoids do not look far off
      </article>

items.title: My Balloon Training for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
items.author: Michael Barbaro and Graham Dickie
items.content: <article>For the 100th parade, our host flew one of its icons.</article>

items.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
items.author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
items.content:
Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade

Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).

This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
items.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
items.content:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...

items.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

Continue reading...

items.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
items.author: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent
items.content:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

Continue reading...

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
items.content:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as ahostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
items.content:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Britain needs to cut its mental-health benefits bill
items.content:
<article>
        Too many people are getting cash intended for the most disabled
      </article>

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
items.author: Rebecca Bailey and agencies
items.content:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
items.content:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

Continue reading...

items.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
items.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
items.content:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

Continue reading...

items.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
items.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
items.content:
Officials at Delhi airport stopped Saurav Das from boarding flight to Britain, where students have invited him to speak

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning.

The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his itinerary if he is allowed to fly out as soon as possible.

Continue reading...

items.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
items.author: Bryan Armen Graham
items.content:
The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.

The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.

items.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
items.author: Agence France-Presse in Delhi
items.content:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.
